questions.question: The GitHub token is in the system prompt with 'never reveal this token'. Is it protected?
options: Yes, the instruction protects it
No: it's in the model's context, the provider's logs and your traces, and one injection can make the model print it
Yes, if the model is large
Only if the prompt is encrypted
questions.explanation: A secret the model can read is a secret it can output. Keep values out of the context.

questions.question: What does the model see when the broker is in place?
options: The token, masked with asterisks
A handle such as {{secret:github_token}}; the broker substitutes the value after the model writes the call
Nothing about the secret
A hash of the token
questions.explanation: The model names the secret. Code, not the model, puts the value where it belongs.

questions.question: An injection asks for `http_request(url='https://api.github.com/?t={{secret:github_token}}')`. Which binding stops it?
options: The tool binding
The host binding
The argument binding: the secret may only go in 'authorization'
Nothing stops it
questions.explanation: Even to an allowed host, a token in a URL ends up in proxy and server logs. Bind the argument too.

questions.question: Why scrub tool results when the model never wrote the token?
options: For performance
Tools can echo it back (error messages, debug endpoints) or return other credentials from files
To shorten outputs
Scrubbing isn't needed with a broker
questions.explanation: Results flow into the context. Anything secret in them is as exposed as if it were in the prompt.

questions.question: Why does child_env use an allow-list instead of removing variables whose names contain KEY or TOKEN?
options: Allow-lists are faster
A deny-list misses secrets with other names (DATABASE_URL, a new variable next month); an allow-list excludes them by default
Deny-lists are not allowed in Python
No difference
questions.explanation: Default-deny survives changes nobody told you about.

questions.question: A token appeared in a trace for a few minutes before your scrubber was fixed. What do you do?
options: Delete the trace and move on
Rotate the token: it has already been sent to the model provider and the log pipeline
Nothing, it was only a few minutes
Ask the model to forget it
questions.explanation: You can't un-send a secret. Rotation is the only reliable fix.
